correctness.rationale: The admissible set is compact and the triangle inequality bounds each distance by 3. A maximizing triple with minimum 3 forces both distances 3; norming dual functionals then expose x and z_i=-y_i/2 on a common face, with separation at least 1. The converse is an explicit triple y_i=-2z_i and norming functional equality. For clipped disks the only positive-length exposed faces are vertical with gauge diameter 2sqrt(1-a^2), giving exactly sqrt(3)/2. The modulus zero threshold uses equality for a boundary midpoint and gives sqrt(15)/4. For the regular even polygon the maximal face-star diameter is the two-step chord norm 2sin(2pi/N) (N divisible by 4) or 4sin(pi/N) (N congruent 2 mod 4), with edge norms no larger; direct monotonicity gives equality exactly through N=12 and strictness starting N=14. An independent exact-rational and floating-point checker returned VERIFY_OK; finite checks are not the proof. Boundary cases a=1 and N=12 are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2026 originating article defines the exact same Rado dilation functional and states the relevant upper and modulus bounds, but not its equality classification or either sharp cutoff. The closest published regular-polygon two-disk source was inspected through its complete primary RESULT.md and instead concerns a different Euclidean continuous two-center problem, with an incompatible objective and normalization. Searches of both existing own weekly ledgers and published-finding corpus for equivalent formulations, support face equality, two-center parameters, clipped disks, regular polygons, and stronger general bounds did not reveal an implication subsuming this exact theorem. Triangle-equality geometry is classical, and an unindexed equivalent special result remains a genuine originality risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed equality-in-the-triangle-inequality characterizations in finite-dimensional Banach geometry might already be phrased as a two-ball saturation criterion.
The external index cannot prove uniqueness, and no claim is made about unpublished work.
The strict <3 classifications give no explicit quantitative gap away from saturation.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact equality classification for a newly motivated all-dimensional dilation functional governing a Radó covering step, not merely a boundary/tiny perturbation check. The geometric criterion replaces a one-sided uniform-convexity sufficient condition with a necessary and sufficient test, and it resolves whole nontrivial infinite families: the strip-clipped disk has the exact phase boundary a=sqrt(3)/2, and regular even polygons change from saturated at N=12 to strict at N=14. Crucially, the open interval sqrt(3)/2<a<=sqrt(15)/4 is a qualitative strict-improvement regime invisible to the originating modulus estimate, showing a real structural distinction between face diameters 1 and 1/2. This motivates the precise threshold and explains how nonuniformly convex norms may still improve the factor. The work does not claim a better universal planar numerical constant.
